extraFacts.fact: Unit conversions (1 bar = 14.5038 psi): 100 psi = about 7 bar; 120 psi = about 8 bar; 125 psi = about 9 bar; 140 psi = about 10 bar; 145 psi = 10 bar; 150 psi = about 10 bar; 200 psi = about 14 bar; 246 psi = about 17 bar; 250 psi = about 17 bar; 300 psi = about 21 bar; 350 psi = about 24 bar; 500 psi = about 34 bar. Temperature (°C = (°F - 32) / 1.8): -40°F = -40°C; -32°F = -36°C; -25°F = -32°C; -10°F = -23°C; -4°F = -20°C; 0°F = -18°C; 15°F = -9°C; 23°F = -5°C; 32°F = 0°C; 122°F = 50°C; 140°F = 60°C; 150°F = 66°C; 158°F = 70°C; 160°F = 71°C; 176°F = 80°C; 200°F = 93°C; 350°F = 177°C; 400°F = 204°C; 450°F = 232°C.
extraFacts.source: NIST SP 811 unit conversion; 1 bar = 14.5038 psi

extraFacts.fact: NPT is the American taper pipe thread to ASME B1.20.1 and NPTF is the dryseal version to ASME B1.20.3; BSPP (G) is parallel pipe thread to ISO 228-1 and BSPT (R) is taper pipe thread to ISO 7-1. NPT and BSP threads do not mate. FNPT is female NPT and MNPT is male NPT.
extraFacts.source: ASME B1.20.1; ASME B1.20.3; ISO 228-1; ISO 7-1

extraFacts.fact: HS 2022 heading 84.81 covers taps, cocks and valves: subheading 8481.20 valves for oleohydraulic or pneumatic transmissions, 8481.30 check (non-return) valves, 8481.40 safety or relief valves, 8481.80 other appliances. The importing country's tariff fixes the final national digits.
ISO 4414 sets the general rules and safety requirements for pneumatic fluid power systems, including that stored pressure be able to be isolated and exhausted before work on the machine.
extraFacts.source: ISO 4414:2010 Pneumatic fluid power - General rules and safety requirements for systems and their components

extraFacts.fact: A check (non-return) valve lets air flow in one direction only; on a compressor discharge line an in-tank check valve sits at the receiver inlet so the tank cannot back-flow into the pump. A pilot unloader check valve combines a check valve with an unloader port that vents the compressor head when it stops.
extraFacts.source: Compressor accessory practice; WCO HS 2022 heading 84.81 (check valves 8481.30)

extraFacts.fact: SCFM means standard cubic feet per minute of free air; it is the flow rating shown in the row text of each Conrader check valve.
extraFacts.source: Compressed Air and Gas Institute (CAGI) terminology

extraFacts.fact: Conrader in-tank check valve inlet types seen in the rows: FNPT (female NPT), Compression, and SAE flare; outlet is male NPT (MNPT). A minimum pressure check valve holds back flow until inlet pressure reaches a set minimum, listed in the CMP rows as 50 to 80 psi or 50 to 70 psi.
extraFacts.source: Conrader CAC, CTA, CTB, CTD, CTF, CTL and CMP series row descriptions (Indus size tables)

faqs.q: What is the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve used for?
faqs.a: Conrader CAC series in-tank check valves are compression-inlet check valves that fit in the receiver inlet of a compressor and stop air flowing back to the pump. The listing has 4 part numbers rated 20 SCFM: CAC1212, CAC3812, CAC3812-NF and CAC3812-SU3-T.

faqs.q: What do Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve part numbers such as CAC3812 mean?
faqs.a: Read the digits as inlet then outlet size: CAC1212 is a 1/2 inch compression inlet with a 1/2 inch male NPT outlet, and CAC3812 is 3/8 inch inlet with 1/2 inch outlet. NF and SU3-T are option suffixes on the 3812 body.

faqs.q: What sizes does the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve come in?
faqs.a: There are two inlet sizes, 1/2 inch (CAC1212) and 3/8 inch (CAC3812 and its two variants), both with a 1/2 inch male NPT outlet and a 20 SCFM rating.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve?
faqs.a: Pick the compression inlet to match your discharge tube (3/8 inch or 1/2 inch) and the 1/2 inch outlet to the tank. For higher flow step up to the [CTA series](/p/conrader-cta-series-in-tank-check-valves).

faqs.q: What pressure and temperature rating does the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve have?
faqs.a: The listing is rated 20 SCFM on every row. A maker pressure and temperature rating is not held for the CAC series here, so we do not state one; ask us for the Conrader data.

faqs.q: What is the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve made of?
faqs.a: The listing does not record the body or seat material of the CAC series; ask us for the specification of your part number. Ask us to confirm the material of the exact part number and the media it will see, because compatibility depends on the fluid, the temperature and the seal.

faqs.q: Does the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve come with certificates?
faqs.a: We hold no certificate data for the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve, so none is claimed here. Ask for a certificate of conformity or origin with your enquiry for CAC3812 and we will tell you what can be supplied.

faqs.q: What connects to the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve?
faqs.a: The compression inlet takes the discharge tube and the male NPT outlet screws into the tank. Pipe fittings are on our [pneumatic fittings shelf](/c/pneumatic-fittings-silencers) and receivers relate to our [air preparation shelf](/c/air-preparation-frl).

faqs.q: How do you install the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve?
faqs.a: Fit the valve at the tank inlet with the flow arrow toward the tank, tighten the compression nut on the tube and drain the tank before removal.

faqs.q: How does the Conrader CAC series in-tank check valve differ from its sibling listings?
faqs.a: The CAC has a compression inlet, while the [CTA series](/p/conrader-cta-series-in-tank-check-valves) has a female NPT inlet and the CTD adds more compression sizes. Send us your duty, pressure and flow and we will confirm which of the two suits the application better.
